claim: Import a reference/background image while already locked to a standard orthographic view (Numpad 1 Front, 3 Side, 7 Top), not from an arbitrary perspective angle, and use (or verify) the 'Align to View' import option -- this guarantees the imported reference plane sits perfectly flat along a standard Cartesian plane (XY/XZ/YZ) with no perspective distortion or accidental tilt, so its 2D dimensions correspond directly to 3D spatial axes without needing manual rotation correction afterward.
supporting_evidence: Gemini video-understanding observation (2026-08-14, watched full video): at 0:48-2:24, an image is imported (Shift+A -> Image -> Reference) while in Front Orthographic view (Numpad 1), with the 'Align to View' toggle demonstrated against the alternative of importing at an arbitrary perspective angle.
rejected_alternative: Importing a reference image while in a free perspective viewport angle, then manually rotating/aligning it afterward
reason: Importing already-orthographic-aligned avoids a manual rotation-correction step and the risk of a subtly-wrong tilt that would silently throw off every subsequent multi-view vertex placement.

claim: A reference image empty's Depth setting (Default/Front/Back) controls whether the 2D reference renders in front of or behind 3D geometry regardless of actual spatial depth ordering: set to Back so opaque mesh geometry doesn't obstruct the guide lines while blocking out a form, or set to Front (paired with reduced Opacity) to overlay reference line art on top of dense/complex geometry for precise silhouette tracing.
supporting_evidence: Gemini video-understanding observation: at 3:20-4:09, the reference empty's Depth property is toggled between Default/Front/Back in Object Data Properties -- Back keeps 3D geometry fully visible in front of the reference, Front overlays the reference line art on top of the geometry.
rejected_alternative: Leaving Depth on Default and accepting whichever occlusion order happens to result from actual spatial position
reason: As a model develops volume, the reference plane's actual spatial position relative to the growing mesh becomes an unreliable predictor of which one should be visually on top -- Depth lets the artist choose the useful occlusion order directly instead of fighting actual depth ordering.

claim: For a multi-view reference setup (front/side/top/rear reference cards), uncheck 'Perspective' under the reference empty's 'Show In' setting so each reference plane only displays while in an orthographic view, not in free perspective navigation -- this keeps perspective-mode viewport navigation uncluttered by floating/intersecting reference planes while still automatically surfacing the correct blueprint the moment the view snaps to a standard orthographic angle (Numpad 1/3/7).
supporting_evidence: Gemini video-understanding observation: at 5:11-5:38, 'Perspective' is unchecked under the reference empty's 'Show In' settings (leaving only 'Orthographic' active), with Opacity also reduced for semi-transparency.
rejected_alternative: Leaving reference images visible in both perspective and orthographic view modes for a multi-card (front/side/top/rear) setup
reason: Multiple intersecting reference cards left visible in perspective mode clutter free-viewport navigation and obstruct inspecting the 3D form directly; restricting display to orthographic-only keeps them out of the way exactly when they're least useful and present exactly when they're needed.

claim: Move all reference-image empties into their own dedicated collection (e.g. named 'References') and disable the Selectable restriction toggle for that collection in the Outliner -- this prevents reference planes from being accidentally box-selected or clicked instead of the actual mesh geometry during modeling, without needing to hide or delete them.
supporting_evidence: Gemini video-understanding observation: at 5:40-7:03, all reference empties are moved (M) into a new 'References' collection, and the Selectable filter toggle for that collection is disabled in the Outliner's restriction toggles.
rejected_alternative: Leaving reference-image empties selectable in the same collection/selection pool as the actual mesh geometry
reason: Reference planes sit spatially close to and often behind the mesh being modeled, making them an easy accidental target for box-select or click-select during normal editing -- an unselectable dedicated collection removes that failure mode entirely rather than relying on the artist to always click precisely.

claim: When a single reference sheet contains multiple orthographic views (front/side/top/rear) that are NOT already centered on a shared origin, duplicate the sheet once per view, rotate each copy onto its correct axis (90/180 degrees as needed), then translate each copy so all views align to the same shared landmark features across views (e.g. a common ground plane at Z=0, a shared centerline) -- this is required before multi-view box-modeling or a Mirror modifier will work correctly, since each view's own drawing rarely starts pre-aligned to a 3D coordinate origin the way the artist needs.
supporting_evidence: Gemini video-understanding observation: at 8:16-10:45, a single blueprint sheet with front/side/top/rear drawings is duplicated per view, rotated onto each respective axis, and translated so all views share common landmarks (tire contact patch at Z=0 ground level, vehicle symmetry line on the vertical axis).
rejected_alternative: Placing each view's reference image at whatever position it happens to import at, without aligning them to shared landmarks across views
reason: If front/side/top reference views aren't calibrated to the same shared origin and landmarks, a vertex placed to match the front view will not line up with the same feature in the side/top views, breaking the whole premise of multi-view modeling and making a Mirror modifier produce an asymmetric result.
